answer: Stake-proportional selection. Agents that wander to map lotus coverage lock funds for a fixed audit horizon. The verifier checks each deposit and gives it sampling weight equal to its locked amount, using an unpredictable epoch seed. The same funds cannot back simultaneous entries. Splitting stake S across N accounts preserves total weight S, so extra identities add no expected reward; more weight requires more locked capital and its opportunity cost. This assumes linear rewards without per-account bonuses and no seed grinding.
